subject: Clarification on which coefficients of CFA with ordered indicators are probit

messages.author: edceb8dce9472a62
messages.subject: Clarification on which coefficients of CFA with ordered indicators are probit
parts:
Hello, 

I have 3 dichotomous indicators of a latent factor. I then regress this latent factor onto some covariates. 

Which part of this model will use probit coefficients, just the loadings of the manifest onto their latent factor? 

The regression from the covariates to the latent variable will not be a probit coefficient, correct?

Here's a simplified piece of syntax to show the example:

mod1 <- 

'

Latent =~ ind1 + ind2 + ind3

Latent ~ covariate + covariate2

'

fit <- cfa.mi(mod1, data = dat_imputed, estimator = 'WLSMV', ordered = c('ind1', 'ind2', 'ind3'))
summary(fit)

Thank you,
Chris

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Clarification on which coefficients of CFA with ordered indicators are probit
parts: Which part of this model will use probit coefficients, just the loadings of the manifest onto their latent factor?
Yes, any outcome that is discrete will be linked to its predictors via a probit function.
The regression from the covariates to the latent variable will not be a probit coefficient, correct?

There are many latent variables in your model (e.g., one latent item-response per dichotomous outcome).  The common factor is assumed normally distributed so it is linked to predictors via the identity function (i.e., regular linear effects as you would find in OLS regression).
